kurz: Crispy is a dry, firm surface that breaks when you bite instead of bending.
bild_im_kopf: Like crackers and bread: almost the same ingredients, but the cracker has no water. That is why it breaks.
bedeutung: Crispiness forms when a thin outer layer of starch or protein loses its water and hardens. If water stays in or steam comes back, the layer turns bendy and soft again.
was_passiert: First the water on the surface has to evaporate. Only then does the temperature rise above 100 °C, and the layer dries out and browns. A rough surface has more area that can turn crisp. A thin film of fat carries heat evenly to every spot.
warum_wichtig: Wedges, chips, rösti, poultry skin, breadcrumb coatings and bread crust: the same goal with the same levers.
faustregeln: Water is the enemy: pat dry, leave space, do not cover.
A rough surface beats a smooth one.
Start hot enough that the water is gone quickly.
After cooking, put it on a rack rather than stacking it: steam from below makes it soft.
typische_fehler: Overloading the tray or pan: the pieces steam each other.
Covering freshly baked food to keep it warm.

praxis.text: Soak, dry well, spread out on a hot tray. Or parboil and roughen.
Leave the skin uncovered in the fridge overnight to dry, then roast or fry it hot.
Fry twice: first to cook, then at high heat to dry the crust.
Steam first for [[ofentrieb|oven spring]], then let the steam out and finish baking dry.

mythos.richtig: A thin film is enough for the heat to reach everywhere. Too much oil makes it greasy, not crispier.
